title: lore check reports a duplicate ADR ordinal as an ERROR naming both files (DEC-180 (1))
description: DEC-180 (1), accepted 2026-10-13 (opum-doc). Measured: `lore new adr` numbers from the working tree alone (nextAdrNumber, src/commands/new.ts:312), reading no ref, worktree or remote. Two branches that each create an ADR get different slugs (for example 0010-alpha.md and 0010-beta.md), so a duplicate ordinal merges SILENTLY with no conflict. `lore check` has no ADR-ordinal rule today (src/core/check.ts), so nothing catches it. Add an error-severity finding that groups docs/adr files by their leading numeric ordinal and reports an ERROR naming BOTH files when two share one. Compare ordinals NUMERICALLY (parse the ^(\d+)- prefix as an integer, as nextAdrNumber does), never lexicographically. The pair must make `lore check` exit 6. Wording (team-lead, 2026-10-13): the message names both files in a stable order and the duplicated ordinal, and does NOT name a command that does not yet exist — word the fix in prose (see the note). The part (2) `lore adr renumber` follow-up criterion is carried in the notes. Prove both ways with predicted mutation arms.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A bundle whose ADRs share an ordinal — same leading number, different slugs (e.g. adr/0010-alpha.md and adr/0010-beta.md) — makes `lore check` report an error-severity finding that names BOTH file paths in a stable order and states the duplicated ordinal, and the command exits 6. The message does not name any command; it words the fix in prose.

Distinct ordinals pass: `lore check` reports no ordinal finding and exits 0 for a bundle whose ADRs are 0009-… and 0010-…, and again for 0099-… and 0100-… — the comparison is numeric (9!=10 and 99!=100), not lexicographic.

Both directions are proved with a predicted mutation arm: replacing the numeric ordinal comparison with a string comparison turns a predicted fixture red (the duplicate the string compare misses), and with the numeric comparison restored the same-ordinal fixture fails and the distinct-ordinal fixtures pass. The predicted outcome and the observed result are recorded.

implementationNotes: Team-lead terms for DEC-180 (1), 2026-10-13. Wording (execution detail, team-lead call): the error names BOTH files in a stable order and the duplicated ordinal, and never names a command that does not exist yet; word the fix in prose, e.g. "renumber one of them to the next free ordinal and update its links". CARRY-FORWARD: when part (2) `lore adr renumber` ships, a criterion on that future task must require this duplicate-ordinal message to name the command. Lifecycle: task before branch; branch feat/LCLI-712-<slug>; about 400 lines; land on dev only, never promote; land on the first approve (a round after a non-approval is a FULL review with base set; confirmatory-only review only after two non-approvals). Report measured context (input + cache_read + cache_creation from the newest usage record) with the PR.
